facts.statement: Unlike more derived aetosaurs, Aetosaurus had a long and narrow carapace that lacked spikes.
facts.quote: Unlike more derived aetosaurs such as Desmatosuchus or Typothorax, the carapace was long and narrow and lacked spikes.

facts.statement: The paramedian scutes covering the back of Aetosaurus were considerably wider than they were long.
facts.quote: The paramedian scutes that covered the back (with one row on each side of the vertebrae) are considerably wider than they are long.

facts.statement: The lateral scutes of Aetosaurus did not bear any spikes or other projections.
facts.quote: The lateral scutes, which are beneath the paramedian and formed a row on either side of the animal, do not bear any spikes or other projections.

facts.statement: Aetosaurus was first named and described in 1877 by the German paleontologist Oscar Fraas.
facts.quote: Aetosaurus was first named, with the description of the type species A. ferratus, in 1877 by German paleontologist Oscar Fraas.

facts.statement: When first described, Aetosaurus was known from 22 articulated skeletons found in the Lower Stubensandstein of Germany.
facts.quote: At the time, Aetosaurus was known from 22 articulated skeletons that had been found in the Lower Stubensandtein of Germany.

facts.statement: Thirty years after the initial description, Eberhard Fraas described the second species, A. crassicauda, from Germany.
facts.quote: Thirty years later, Fraas' son Eberhard described a second species, A. crassicauda, also from Germany.

facts.statement: Specimens of Aetosaurus occur in strata dating to the Norian age.
facts.quote: Specimens of Aetosaurus occur in Norian-age strata.

facts.statement: Aetosaurus lived between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago during the Norian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Three species are currently recognized: A. ferratus from Germany and Italy, A. crassicauda from Germany, and A. arcuatus from eastern North America.
facts.quote: Three species are currently recognized: A. ferratus, the type species from Germany and Italy; A. crassicauda from Germany; and A. arcuatus from eastern North America.

facts.statement: In 1998, the genus Stegomus was synonymized with Aetosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1998, the genus Stegomus was synonymized with Aetosaurus.

facts.statement: In 1896, Othniel Charles Marsh named Stegomus arcuatus based on a cast of an aetosaur known as YPM 1647 from the New Haven Formation.
facts.quote: In 1896, paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh named Stegomus arcuatus from a cast of an aetosaur known as YPM 1647 from the New Haven Formation in the Fair Haven Heights neighborhood of New Haven.

facts.statement: Aetosaurus belongs to the family Stagonolepididae.
Aetosaurus belongs to the subfamily Aetosaurinae.

facts.statement: The carapace of Aetosaurus is "waisted", meaning it narrows in front of the pelvis.
facts.quote: El caparazón está "entallado", lo que significa que se estrecha delante de la pelvis.
